claims.statement: The proposed paid event is a recurring cover fee and the defined loss event is a weather-adjusted efficiency or comfort miss; neither customer willingness nor loss frequency is yet evidenced.
Installers or property owners are the hypothesised payers because heat pumps are installed and maintained as building systems, but no budget interviews or purchase commitments exist.
The only plausible founder control path is explicit site data consent plus an installer service contract and a separate risk-capital agreement; none is currently executed.
The European Commission describes heat pumps as mature, efficient building technology and EU building policy creates a long-run renovation context, but that does not validate a warranty business.

commercial_mechanics.budget_owner: Installer owner or service director, building owner, or portfolio asset manager
commercial_mechanics.bundling_resistance: Offer vendor-neutral measurement, separate diagnosis from remediation, and publish auditable contract thresholds that survive installer or OEM changes
commercial_mechanics.customer_relationship_owner: The installer before a direct site agreement is executed

fully_loaded_economics.acquisition_cost: Installer onboarding and sales share; target below 400 PLN per activated site
fully_loaded_economics.cash_conversion: Fees collected monthly or annually in advance; claim reserves or carrier remittance constrain usable cash
fully_loaded_economics.contribution_margin: Monitoring-only target 55-75%; risk-bearing margin cannot be estimated before loss-frequency data and carrier terms
fully_loaded_economics.delivery_and_support_costs: Remote monitoring plus exception-driven diagnosis; field remediation remains with contracted installers
fully_loaded_economics.overhead_and_compliance: Contract design, consumer law, data protection, cyber security, insurance-regulatory advice, accounting, and liability cover
fully_loaded_economics.revenue_basis: Hypothesis: 25-60 PLN per site per month for measurement and administration plus an actuarially priced risk premium retained by a carrier
fully_loaded_economics.variable_costs: Gateway/API fees, weather data, inspections, service credits, carrier share, payment fees, and support

commercial_mechanics.likely_incumbent_response: OEMs and large installers can extend warranties, expose proprietary diagnostics, or bundle monitoring into maintenance plans
commercial_mechanics.paid_event_or_measurable_loss: Recurring administration premium is paid per covered system; the measurable loss is a contractually specified service credit, remediation cost, or excess energy cost after a weather-adjusted performance miss
commercial_mechanics.payer: Installer, property owner, housing manager, or authorised risk carrier
commercial_mechanics.purchase_trigger: An installer needs to reduce sales friction and post-install disputes, or an owner wants a measurable outcome rather than an equipment-only warranty
commercial_mechanics.renewal_event: Cover renews after a season of adequate telemetry and acceptable claims experience

contrary_evidence: Modern heat pumps already carry equipment warranties, and some installers may view independent measurement as a source of disputes rather than a sales aid.
Building-envelope quality and occupant behaviour may make a simple performance promise too noisy to price economically.

critical_control_point.acquisition_instrument: Proposed site-specific data-rights consent plus installer service agreement and, for insured risk, a carrier or coverholder agreement
critical_control_point.counterparty_refusal_fallback: Sell monitoring and root-cause reporting without risk transfer, accept customer-exported meter data, or integrate another compatible device vendor
critical_control_point.current_owner: Homeowner controls consent; installers and device vendors may separately control portions of the source data
critical_control_point.customer_relationship_owner: The installer before a direct site agreement is executed
critical_control_point.duration: Proposed 24-month cover term; source-data availability and consent duration are unverified
critical_control_point.founder_access_description: The parents' renewable-installation firm could lawfully test measurement and reporting with consenting customers, but it supplies no present data rights, insurance authority, or exclusive distribution.
critical_control_point.launch_controller: Homeowner, installer, relevant device data holder, and any regulated risk carrier
critical_control_point.renewal: Annual renewal after claims and telemetry review
critical_control_point.subject: Right to ingest and use installation, indoor-temperature, energy, weather, and service-event data for a covered site

economics.acquisition_route: Installer-attached opt-in at quotation or annual service, beginning with a small lawful family-firm pilot
economics.founder_net_worth_path: Recurring cover administration across installer portfolios could reach strategic scale; a 5m PLN outcome would require carrier-backed expansion and tens of thousands of covered systems over roughly 4-7 years
economics.founder_time: Up to five hours per day with automated monitoring and installer-delivered field remediation
economics.gross_margin_basis: Monitoring fee less telemetry, support, inspections, installer share, carrier share, and expected service-credit cost
economics.payback: Target under twelve months on installer integration and site hardware; not evidenced
economics.pricing: Hypothesis: 25-60 PLN per site per month for monitoring and administration; risk premium quoted separately by an authorised partner
economics.retention_or_repeat: Annual renewal if the site keeps compatible telemetry and values dispute prevention or outcome assurance

fingerprint.compounding_advantage: A consented dataset linking system design, weather, controls, service actions, and outcomes improves pricing and root-cause triage
fingerprint.customer: Heat-pump installers and small portfolios of building owners that need outcome assurance
fingerprint.distribution_mechanism: Installers attach the offer at quotation, commissioning, or annual service
fingerprint.offer_and_business_model: Telemetry-backed performance administration with optional carrier-backed warranty cover, priced per installed system
fingerprint.payer_and_paid_event: Installer or building owner pays a recurring cover and monitoring fee; a defined service credit is triggered by verified seasonal underperformance
fingerprint.problem_trigger: A buyer cannot distinguish equipment defects from sizing, commissioning, control, weather, or building-envelope causes when bills or comfort disappoint

founder_fit: Combines statistical baselining, anomaly detection, energy systems, and commercial contract analysis
A family installer relationship permits a lawful measurement pilot without implying access to customers or private data
Monitoring and claim triage can be automated and operated alongside employment before risk is assumed
Capital exposure can remain below the founder limit by starting as monitoring software and using a licensed carrier
risks: Mispriced outcome cover could exceed the founder's capital rapidly
Consent withdrawal or OEM API closure could break measurement continuity
Incorrect diagnosis could create consumer, safety, and installer-liability exposure
Incumbent OEMs may bundle superior device telemetry with extended warranties

structural_signature.commercial_model_descriptor: performance cover administration with optional carrier backed service credits
structural_signature.control_point_descriptor: consented weather normalized heat pump performance and claims history
structural_signature.critical_dependency_descriptor: licensed carrier warranty obligor or ring fenced reserve for promised payouts

structure.control_point: consented longitudinal commissioning and performance dataset
structure.critical_dependency: risk-bearing capital or an authorised carrier willing to bind the defined cover

thesis: Future operating state (2031): heat-pump retrofits are sold with a seasonal comfort-and-efficiency outcome rather than only an equipment warranty. Missing financial and data mechanism: a defensible weather-adjusted baseline, consented telemetry, claims rules, and a reserve or authorised risk carrier that can fund service credits when the promised outcome is missed.
title: Measured Heat-Pump Outcome Cover
uncertainties: Whether the product is legally an insurance contract, warranty, service guarantee, or unregulated monitoring service in Poland
Minimum sensor set and baseline period needed for a fair seasonal outcome
Loss frequency, severity, adverse selection, and carrier appetite
Installer and homeowner willingness to grant reliable telemetry access
